pairs.subject: settings
pairs.evidence: src/lib/db/org-registry.ts:218 The registry's per-org configuration (mode, telemetrySink) is overwritten in place by an upsert that keeps no old value, category or origin record, and the read mapper drops an unrecognised stored value back to the default without reporting it, so 'who turned telemetry on, and what was it before' has no answer and a corrupted column reads as a deliberate choice.

techniques.evidence: src/lib/db/org-registry.ts:218 A re-map overwrites mode/telemetrySink with no key/old/new/origin record. The route keeps only createdBy and has no audit call (grepped 'audit' in route.ts and org-registry.ts: no hits).

src/lib/db/org-registry.ts:102 The read clamp to a closed enum is there, but an unknown stored value silently becomes the default with no corruption report. The column is a free String (schema.prisma:1717), so this can happen. The write door is conformant: route.ts:49 rejects anything outside the closed set with a 400.

src/features/shared/registry/registryActionRules.ts:91 The telemetry sink acts like an opt-in flag and defaults to off. The view repeats that floor (registry-view.ts:333 `sink: row?.telemetrySink ?? "off"`).

src/features/shared/registry/useRegistryMutation.ts:80 Explicit submit. Choices stay in local form state (no optimistic flip). A failure shows inline next to the control, and only a success runs router.refresh() to re-read stored truth (line 85).
prisma/schema.prisma:1717 These settings are fixed typed columns on one row, not a free-string key space, so typo and orphan keys cannot occur.

pairs.registryProposal: The standard assumes a key-value store. Many apps keep per-entity configuration as typed columns on a domain row (here: OrgRegistry.mode/telemetrySink). Typed-accessors and settings-audit still apply there, but key-registry and read-batching do not. A sentence on 'settings as columns of a domain row' would make that boundary explicit.
